summary: A Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University and taught Satoshi Hiraoka.

A Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held posts at Rissho University (~1971–1982), Shinshu University (professor ~1982–1988, emeritus ~1995), and Mejiro University (~1988–1999).

A scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and historical studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1977) and Osaka University. He held posts at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Kanazawa University, and Osaka University (professor ~1992–2013).

A religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1952–1960). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1964–1997) and served as president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions in 1997.
A Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University in 2014.

A scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg under Akira Hirakawa and Albrecht Wezler. He served as assistant professor and professor at Waseda University from ~1987 to 2015.
A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University. He was attested as a lecturer at Taisho University in 1995 and 2006.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Rissho University (~1950–1954) and later served there as emeritus professor (~2002–2020).
A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Komazawa University (~1980–1986) and Peking University (~1986–1988). He became an assistant professor at Komazawa University in ~1993.
A sinology and religious studies scholar who studied at Hosei University and served as an assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto around 1994.
A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University, attested between 1978–1981 and in 1991.
A Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979 and served as an assistant at Taisho University in 1978.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Delhi (attested 1996). He held posts at Tohoku University, National Institute of Technology Sendai College, and Hosen Gakuen College.

An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. In 1995, he held posts as a lecturer at Taisho University and researcher at the Buzan-ha Institute of Modern Mission.
A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1995) and became a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University around 2002.
A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University (~1967–1976) and later served there as professor (~1990–2017).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as a group member and later as professor (attested 2014) at Taisho University.
A sinology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1935–1938). He held posts at Otemon Gakuin University (~1978–1985) and Otemae University (~1985–1990).
An Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1974–1978), where he later taught (~1989–2020). He also taught Kei Kataoka.

A philosophy and Japanology scholar who studied at Kyoto and Nagoya Universities. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University (professor ~1957–1972), the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (director general ~1987–1995), and the Institute of Technologists.
